rebuttals.text: A man who believes he is a woman is not mentally well.
You cannot feel your way into being the opposite sex.
The clinical consensus on trans identity was driven by activism, not new evidence.

because.text: Professional medical bodies face organized pressure to affirm rather than question.

rebuttals.text: Rapid-onset gender dysphoria spreads among teenagers through peer and online networks.
Most children who experience gender dysphoria desist by adulthood when not affirmed.
Gender dysphoria is a diagnosable condition in the DSM-5 and ICD-11.
Affirmation-only care forecloses investigation of the underlying causes of distress.
Every major medical association endorses gender-affirming care as the standard of care.

because.text: The APA, AMA, WPATH, and Endocrine Society all classify it as evidence-based.

rebuttals.text: The DSM-5 removed transgender identity itself as a disorder; only the distress of dysphoria is diagnosable.
Gender identity has measurable neurobiological correlates independent of upbringing.
Interrogating a settled clinical consensus as if it were open is rhetoric, not inquiry.

because.text: The skeptical case reliably arrives at a predetermined policy conclusion.

rebuttals.text: The sex-science argument is a motte-and-bailey: defend that sex is real to smuggle in that trans women are men.
Trans people understand their own identity better than strangers do.
This is cruelty dressed up as concern for the vulnerable.
Gender dysphoria and body dysmorphic disorder both center on distress about one's own body.
Body dysmorphic disorder is a perceived defect in appearance; gender dysphoria is incongruence between identity and sex characteristics.

because.text: The two carry distinct diagnostic criteria and distinct treatments.

rebuttals.text: Treating body dysmorphia reduces the fixation; for gender dysphoria the evidenced treatment is transition.
Biological sex is defined by gamete type: organisms are built to produce either small or large gametes.

because.text: No sexually reproducing species produces a viable third gamete type.

rebuttals.text: The gamete-based definition of sex holds across the sexually reproducing tree of life.
Intersex conditions are disorders of sexual development within the two sexes, not additional sexes.
Anisogamy is a species-level reproductive strategy, not a rule for classifying individuals.

because.text: Prepubescent, infertile, and post-menopausal people have a sex while producing no gametes at all.

rebuttals.text: Biological sex is a cluster of traits — chromosomes, gonads, hormones, and anatomy — that usually align but can dissociate.

because.text: These traits come apart in numerous well-documented conditions of sexual development.

rebuttals.text: A robust sex binary describes populations; it does not fix any individual's gender or social role.
A definition of sex that has to carve out exceptions is not the clean binary it claims to be.
Isogamous species reproduce sexually with no difference in gamete size at all.
